To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the STRF of some midbrain auditory neurons can be used to predict their responses to vocalizations; (2) the STRF is orientation-specific; (3) some midbrain neurons have orientation-specific STRF that can be used for the prediction of responses to vocalizations, and (4) inhibitory areas are important for a good prediction of the cell response to vocalization sounds.

1) FM-sensitive neurons of IC can be modeled as having STRFs with inhibitory areas, 2) STRFs with inhibitions can predict the response of the neurons to the rat's vocalizations, 3) STRFs with inhibition are more accurate than STRFs without inhibitions in predicting the response of IC neurons to vocalizations, and 4) STRFs with and without inhibitions are equally effective in predicting the response to the rat's FM tones.
the STRF with inhibition may account for the response of IC auditory neurons to their vocalization calls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of models of the response of neurons in the midbrain auditory system to vocalization sounds in the rat.
the modeling of auditory neurons in the midbrain of the rat in response to vocalization sounds of conspecifics.
understanding the neural processing of vocalization sounds in the auditory pathway of the mammalian brain.

(1) the STRFs of the FM sensitive IC neurons can be used to predict the responses of these neurons to complex sounds, but (2) the STRFs need to be modified to include inhibitory areas.
the STRF of IC neurons may account for their response to vocalizations sounds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditory midbrain neurons are sensitive to the spectral shape of the sounds, and their responses to vocalizations can be modeled based on their FM sensitivities.
(i) STRF with inhibitions are useful for predicting auditory neuron response to communication calls; and (ii) the STRF with inhibition is a better model for FM-sensitive neurons than the simple STRF.
the STRF model is a useful tool in the study of the auditory system and that inhibitory areas in the model may account for the responses of IC neurons to vocalization sounds.

the STRF can be estimated from the cell's response in a simple FM stimulus.
a single unit's FM sensitivity can be used to infer its STRF and that the inferred STRF can be used to predict the response to a complex vocalization sound.
the STRF can be used to predict the responses of midbrain auditory cells to complex communication signals.
